name: modules.md
html:
The modules — how the whole thing fits

luiskr.com V3 is a monorepo of eight workspace modules — each a git submodule with its own repository, package.json, tsconfig, vite config and Jest suite. This page is the map of the whole: what each module is for, how a request travels through them, and how the codebase documents itself.

The cast

                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │                 shared/                     │
                 │  app shell · orchestrator · build matrix    │
                 │  verify/test/docs pipelines · vendored deps │
                 └───────────────────┬────────────────────────┘
                                     │ mounts & wires
        ┌──────────────┬────────────┼────────────┬──────────────────┐
        ▼              ▼            ▼            ▼                  ▼
     website/       cms/     experiments/    experiments/      desktop/
   public site    admin      docs portal   earth + star-field   Electron
        └──────────────┴────────────┴────────────┴──────────────────┘
                                     │ built on
                                     ▼
                              ┌─────────────┐
                              │    core/    │
                              │ the platform│
                              └─────────────┘
Module Role Story
shared/ The operation — <app-root> shell, workspace registry, 12-tier build matrix, the verify/test/docs toolchain README · portal
core/ The platform — JSX runtime, component base, store, router, i18n, tokens, WebGL widgets, WASM pool README · portal
website/ The public site — home/project/legal/404 views + every component and effect README · portal
cms/ The admin — Firebase editors per content node, localhost media converter, deploy-info viewer README · portal
experiments/docs The docs portal — browsable docs/reports/coverage/source via a lazy manifest README · portal
experiments/earth-playground Earth Playground — WebGPU Earth, atmosphere, moon, post chain, live panel README · portal
experiments/star-field Star Field — Solar System → Milky Way → observable universe; 134 bodies + 139k-record catalog README · portal
desktop/ The shell — Electron wrapper serving dist/ on a local port; per-OS installers README · portal

The shape of a request

  1. index.html boots shared/scripts/build/browser-loader.js — an ES5 script that walks the ES feature ladder newest→oldest and loads the best bundle tier (esnext down to the es2016 IIFE).
  2. The tier's entry runs shared/src/main.ts: side-effect imports (service worker, global styles, router, store, <app-root>), then parallel warm-up — the locale's baked snapshot + the likely route chunk fetch before mount.
  3. The core/ router resolves the localized slug; shared/src/app/view.ts lazy-imports the view chunk — website/views/* for pages, experiments/*/… for the docs portal, playground, or star field.
  4. The view fetches its translations/<locale>/ nodes via the SWR data layer — instant from the bundled snapshot, then a silent Firebase revalidate — renders JSX into its shadow root, mounts children, publishes JSON-LD.
  5. Those same translation nodes are written by cms/ — a separate bundle behind Google OAuth — so content travels CMS → RTDB → site with no deploy.

How crawlers see it

The app is an SPA, but the crawl surface is fully enumerated at build time:

  • generate-sitemap.js mirrors the runtime router + LANG_SLUGS into a sitemap index, per-locale sitemap-<loc>.xml files, urllist.txt, and localized robots.txt / llms.txt / ai-catalog.json — every canonical route, localized slug, portfolio project, and star-field body deep link. Docs routes stay English-only.
  • build-locale-pages.mjs pre-renders each localized route into dist/langs/<loc>/<route>/ — translated <title>/meta/canonical, per-route hreflang alternates, localized JSON-LD — with Firebase rewrites mapping public paths to those documents.
  • shared/tests/governance/seo-route-parity.test.js pins the committed artifacts, firebase.json rewrites, and slug table in sync.

How the docs are made

The repository documents itself in three layers, all browsable at /docs:

  • Curated — the architecture and guide pages you're reading (shared/docs/), plus each module's README.md (published under its source root: /docs/core/README.md, /docs/starfield/README.md, …).
  • Generated — shared/scripts/docs/gen-docs.mjs extracts the @file/@description/@param JSDoc from every source file (1163 pages and counting) — shared/src, shared/build, shared/scripts, core, website, cms, experiments, shared/local-modules, desktop — into per-file markdown under docs/api/ and docs/jsdocs/ (plus typedoc/ and sassdoc/).
  • Source — the docs portal also publishes the raw source trees as syntax-highlighted, comment-bearing pages (the src:, shared:, core:, website:, cms:, earth:, starfield:, docs-exp:, desktop: and local-modules: roots), lazily fetched per file via docs-content/*.json — with per-module Istanbul coverage reports under coverage-*:.

So the story is: code comments → generated pages → one lazy portal. The comments live in the source; gen-docs.mjs turns them into the API tree; shared/build/docs/ (scan → render → redact) turns the whole repo surface — docs, source, reports, coverage — into the manifest the portal browses.

Ownership rules

  • core/ imports nothing from website/, cms/ or experiments/.
  • website/ and cms/ import from core/ only — never each other.
  • experiments/ may import core/; nothing imports them except the app shell's lazy route loader.
  • shared/ orchestrates all of it and owns the tooling every module's hooks, gates and builds run through.
  • Cross-area imports resolve through the path aliases (@core/…, @website/…, @cms/…, @earth/…, @docs/…).

See architecture.md for the deep dive.
